# @zakkster/lite-aabb

> Zero-GC 2D axis-aligned bounding-box primitives. Twenty-two operations on a flat `Float32Array(4)` `[minX, minY, maxX, maxY]`, including packed `4*N` batch ops. Every op that returns a box writes into a caller-provided `out` buffer. ~230 lines, zero deps, ESM only.

## Format

An AABB is a `Float32Array` of length 4. Indices: `0=minX`, `1=minY`, `2=maxX`, `3=maxY`. No class wrapper; module-level functions only.

## Format contract

The `Float32Array(4)` layout is a versioned, cross-package contract shared with `@zakkster/lite-bvh`, documented in `FORMAT.md` and advertised by `FORMAT_VERSION` (integer, `1`). Both packages export the same `FORMAT_VERSION` and compare it for equality to detect a format skew; it is on a separate axis from the semver `VERSION`.

## API

Named exports: `aabb2`, `VERSION`, `FORMAT_VERSION`.

```ts
aabb2.create(minX?, minY?, maxX?, maxY?): Float32Array  // ALLOCATES — setup only
aabb2.clone(a): Float32Array                            // ALLOCATES — setup only
aabb2.copy(out, a): out                                 // out ← a
aabb2.set(out, minX, minY, maxX, maxY): out             // write explicit bounds
aabb2.merge(out, a, b): out                             // out ← bbox enclosing a∪b
aabb2.extend(out, b): out                               // out grows in place to include b
aabb2.fatten(out, a, margin): out                       // expand by margin on all sides
aabb2.perimeter(a): number                              // 2 * (w + h)
aabb2.area(a): number                                   // w * h
aabb2.overlapArea(a, b): number                         // intersection area, 0 if disjoint, NaN if a NaN coord (v1.1.0+)
aabb2.intersects(a, b): boolean                         // overlap test (touching counts)
aabb2.contains(a, b): boolean                           // a fully contains b (touching counts)
aabb2.isValid(a): boolean                               // finite x4 AND min<=max (v1.1.0+)
aabb2.isEmpty(a): boolean                               // a === [Inf,Inf,-Inf,-Inf] exactly (v1.1.0+)
aabb2.setEmpty(out): out                                // write canonical empty box; merge/extend identity (v1.1.0+)
aabb2.marginFloor(a): number                            // smallest margin that provably widens a; f32 ULP of largest coord (v1.2.0+)
aabb2.containsPoint(a, px, py): boolean                  // point in box, edges included; false on NaN (v1.3.0+)
aabb2.distanceSq(a, b): number                           // squared distance; 0 if overlapping/touching; NaN propagates (v1.3.0+)
aabb2.closestPoint(out2, a, px, py): out2                // closest point on a to (px,py); out2 is LENGTH-2 (Vec2) (v1.3.0+)
aabb2.fattenAll(outPacked, inPacked, margin, count): outPacked  // fatten N packed boxes; in-place or disjoint only (v2.0.0+)
aabb2.mergeAll(out4, inPacked, count): out4              // union of N packed boxes; count 0 -> empty sentinel (v2.0.0+)
aabb2.intersectsAny(inPacked, b, count): index | -1      // first packed box intersecting b (touching counts), else -1 (v2.0.0+)
```

`Packed` is a `Float32Array` of `4*N` floats, box `i` at slots `4i..4i+3`. The batch ops walk it by index -- no per-box `subarray`, zero allocation. `count` bounds every loop (0/negative/NaN -> zero boxes); the caller owns buffer length (`inPacked.length >= 4*count`), and an out-of-range read yields NaN, which propagates.

`Vec2` is a length-2 `Float32Array` `[x, y]`. `closestPoint`'s `out2` is the only length-2 buffer here; every other buffer is a length-4 AABB. Passing a length-4 box as `out2` (or a `Vec2` to a box op) reads/writes the wrong slots and does not throw -- the `out2` name flags the arity at the call site.

## Rules

- `create` and `clone` allocate — call only at initialization.
- Every other function takes an `out` parameter and writes into it. None allocate.
- `out` may alias any input under any view relationship — identical view, a shifted/overlapping `subarray` of one buffer, or a distinct buffer. The writers snapshot inputs before writing (v1.0.2+; ≤1.0.1 corrupted shifted views — finding A-07). This "alias anything" rule holds for the single-box writers and for `mergeAll`/`intersectsAny`; it does NOT extend to `fattenAll`, whose element-wise write forbids a shifted/overlapping `outPacked` (in-place `outPacked === inPacked` or a disjoint buffer only — see `FORMAT.md`).
- The `aabb2` namespace is frozen (`Object.isFrozen(aabb2) === true`); its ops are a contract, not a mutable bag.
- All predicate boundaries are inclusive (touching counts as overlap / contained), EXCEPT `overlapArea`, which returns `0` for a touching (zero-width) intersection — a touching pair shares zero area. This three-way split is deliberate. `containsPoint` follows the inclusive rule (edges/corners count); `distanceSq` is `0` for overlapping AND touching boxes.
- Precision law (v1.2.0+): float32 has a coordinate-dependent step (ULP), so `fatten` silently fails to widen once the margin drops below it (finding A-01: `fatten(o, [1e7,1e7,1e7+1,1e7+1], 0.5)` is a no-op, and `contains` still says true). `fatten` is UNCHANGED -- it never branches or bumps. Instead `marginFloor(a)` reports the smallest margin that provably widens the box (the upper ULP of the largest-magnitude coordinate), and the caller clamps: `fatten(out, a, Math.max(margin, marginFloor(a)))`. Same door-not-hot-op shape as `isValid`. `marginFloor` fails closed: NaN coord -> NaN, infinite coord -> Infinity. Need a larger honest range? Pass your own `Float64Array` out-buffer to the out-param ops (the floor still exists, near ~1e15).
- Degenerate-value law (v1.1.0+): NaN propagates, never launders — a NaN coordinate yields NaN from every numeric op (`area`, `overlapArea`, `distanceSq`, ...); the boolean predicates (`intersects`, `contains`, `containsPoint`) fail closed to `false` instead. Every box is VALID (`isValid`: finite x4 AND min<=max), EMPTY (`isEmpty`: the sentinel `[Inf,Inf,-Inf,-Inf]`, the merge/extend identity, built by `setEmpty`), or GARBAGE. The geometry ops are total and branchless — they do NOT validate; check `isValid` at trust boundaries. The empty sentinel is NOT `isValid` (non-finite by construction; its perimeter/area are -Inf/+Inf) — recognize it with `isEmpty`. Inverted boxes (min>max, e.g. from an over-negative `fatten` margin) have positive `area` and do not self-intersect; that is the caller's bug, detected by `isValid`.
- Use `Float32Array`, not `Array` or `number[]` — typed-array indexed reads are ~3× faster.

## When to use

- Per-frame collision broadphase in canvas / WebGL / WebGPU games.
- Bounds-tracking for sprite batchers, scroll viewports, hit-testing.
- Twitch Extension overlays where any per-frame allocation breaks the 60fps budget.
- Compatible leaf-AABB format for `@zakkster/lite-bvh` (insert / update / query).

## When not to use

- 3D bounding boxes — this is `(minX, minY, maxX, maxY)` only.
- Sub-pixel-stable simulations spanning millions of world units — `Float32` precision (~7 decimal digits) becomes limiting and `fatten` margins evaporate (detect with `marginFloor`); pass your own `Float64Array` out-buffer to push the floor out to ~1e15 and pay the doubled memory.
- Swept-AABB / TOI computation — use a CCD library; this package is for static bounds at a single time step.

## Install

```bash
npm i @zakkster/lite-aabb
```

```js
import { aabb2 } from '@zakkster/lite-aabb';
```
